questions.problem:
Which of the following integers has a multiplicative inverse modulo $42?$

I. $12$

II. $25$

III. $37$
questions.worked_solution:
An integer $a$ has a multiplicative inverse modulo $n$ if and only if $a$ and $n$ are coprime, i.e., $\text{gcd}(a,n)=1.$

With this in mind, let's examine the given options.

- $12$ does *not* have a multiplicative inverse modulo $42$ since $\text{gcd}(12,42)=6\ne 1.\,\,\times $

- $25$ has a multiplicative inverse modulo $42$ since $\text{gcd}(25,42)=1.\,\,✓$

- $37$ has a multiplicative inverse modulo $42$ since $\text{gcd}(37,42)=1.\,\,✓$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."

questions.worked_solution:
The multiplicative inverse of $3$ modulo $8,$ denoted ${3}^{-1},$ is the number $x$ such that

$$
3\cdot x≡1\,(\text{mod}\,8).
$$

Note that since $\text{gcd}(3,8)=1,$ an inverse element exists and is unique up to congruence modulo $8.$

Since the modulus $n=8$ is small, we can find the inverse $x$ by computing exponents of $3$ (modulo $8$) until we get a result of $1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{2} & ≡3\cdot 3≡9≡1\cdot 8+1≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,8)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $3\cdot 3≡1\,(\text{mod}\,8).$ Therefore, the multiplicative inverse of $3$ modulo $8$ is $3.$

questions.worked_solution:
First of all, notice that $\text{gcd}(85,211)=1.$ So, the multiplicative inverse of $85$ modulo $211$ exists.

The multiplicative inverse of $85$ modulo $211$ is the number $x$ such that

$$
85\cdot x≡1\,(\text{mod}\,211).
$$

To find the value of $x,$ we will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}211 & = & 85\cdot 2 & + & 41 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 85 & = & 41\cdot 2 & + & 3 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 41 & = & 3\cdot 13 & + & 2 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 3 & = & 2\cdot 1 & + & 1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Solving for the rightmost terms in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}41 & =211-85\cdot 2 \\ 3 & =85-41\cdot 2 \\ 2 & =41-3\cdot 13 \\ 1 & =3-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =3-2 \\  & =3-(41-3\cdot 13) \\  & =3\cdot 14-41 \\  & =(85-41\cdot 2)\cdot 14-41 \\  & =85\cdot 14-41\cdot 29 \\  & =85\cdot 14-(211-85\cdot 2)\cdot 29 \\  & =85\cdot 72-211\cdot 29 \\  & =85\cdot 72+211\cdot (-29)\end{aligned}
$$

We can write this result modulo $211,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}85\cdot 72+211\cdot (-29) & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,211) \\ 85\cdot 72 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,211)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have $85\cdot 72≡1\,(\text{mod}\,211),$ which means that ${85}^{-1}\,\text{mod}\,211=72.$

questions.worked_solution:
First of all, notice that $\text{gcd}(69,82)=1.$ So, the multiplicative inverse of $69$ modulo $82$ exists.

The multiplicative inverse of $69$ modulo $82$ is the number $x$ such that

$$
69\cdot x≡1\,(\text{mod}\,82).
$$

To find the value of $x,$ we will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}82 & = & 69\cdot 1 & + & 13 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 69 & = & 13\cdot 5 & + & 4 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 13 & = & 4\cdot 3 & + & 1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Solving for the rightmost terms in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}13 & =82-69 \\ 4 & =69-13\cdot 5 \\ 1 & =13-4\cdot 3.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =13-4\cdot 3 \\  & =13-(69-13\cdot 5)\cdot 3 \\  & =13-69\cdot 3+13\cdot 15 \\  & =13\cdot 16-69\cdot 3 \\  & =(82-69)\cdot 16-69\cdot 3 \\  & =82\cdot 16-69\cdot 16-69\cdot 3 \\  & =82\cdot 16-69\cdot 19 \\  & =69\cdot (-19)+82\cdot 16\end{aligned}
$$

We can write this result modulo $82,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}69\cdot (-19)+82\cdot 16 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,82) \\ 69\cdot (-19) & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,82) \\ 69\cdot (82-19) & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,82) \\ 69\cdot 63 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,82)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have $69\cdot 63≡1\,(\text{mod}\,82),$ which means that ${69}^{-1}\,\text{mod}\,82=63.$
